# Hands-on testing guide (v0.4.0)

How to try `legal-redact` yourself, without any real client documents. Everything below uses
**synthetic** fixtures generated by `scripts/make_test_documents.py`; do not test this pre-alpha
tool on real client files yet.

Two ways in:

- **A. The checkout you already have** (`C:\Users\kiril\Projects\legal-redact`) — fastest: its
  `.venv` already has the ML extras, the cached models and Tesseract. Verify it matches the release:
  `git fetch --tags && git log --oneline -1` and check that `git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD`
  prints `v0.3.0`.
- **B. A fresh clone of the published repo** — proves that what is on GitHub installs and works.

## 0. Safety and scope

- Synthetic data only. The fixtures plant fake personal data (`Alice Example`, a fake IBAN, a
  Luhn-valid test card, a DOB, an address) plus lookalikes that must survive (an amount, a contract
  date, a party name, governing law).
- Known limits are listed in [README](../README.md#limitations) and [docs/DOCX.md](DOCX.md). Do not
  report these as bugs: NFD Unicode names, text inside small images, presentation-only Word names,
  tracked changes (refused on purpose), DOCX review being batch-style, `.doc`/`.docm`/encrypted
  files (refused), the `pdfredeval` rendering-condition benchmark (fails closed by scope).

## A. Existing checkout (recommended)

```powershell
cd C:\Users\kiril\Projects\legal-redact
git fetch --tags
git status --short          # expect: clean
git describe --tags --exact-match HEAD   # expect: v0.3.0
```

Confirm the environment (the `.venv` here already has the ML extras and models):
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe --help
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q   # expect: 234 passed (OCR tests skip without Tesseract)
```

## B. Fresh clone (published version)

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/kirillsakhin/legal-redact.git legal-redact-test
cd legal-redact-test
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev]"      # core + dev tools, no model download
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q                    # expect: 234 passed
```

Full detector ensemble (Presidio + GLiNER; needed to test names/addresses; the weights download
once, then everything runs offline):
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e ".[dev,ml]"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m spacy download en_core_web_lg
```

Tesseract 5.x with the `eng` and `osd` training data is optional (scanned PDFs only). `legal-redact
inspect` reports whether it was found; set `TESSERACT_CMD` if it is not on PATH.

## 1. Generate the test documents

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\make_test_documents.py --out testdocs
```

This writes `testdocs\contract.pdf`, `contract-scan.pdf`, `contract-rotated.pdf`, `contract.docx`,
`contract-tracked.docx`, `contract-large-image.docx` and `planted.json` (the planted values: the
"must be removed" list and the "must survive" list). Keep `planted.json` open while testing.

## 2. Track A — PDF with a text layer

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract.pdf
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe review  testdocs\contract.pdf
```

In the review page: accept the 8 suggestions, acknowledge any pre-flight findings, click export.
Then check the result with the checker:

```powershell
# the export path is printed by the page; for the CLI flow it is the -o file
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\check_planted_values.py testdocs\planted.json <exported>.pdf
```

Expect: `PASS` — every "must be removed" value is gone, and the "must survive" lookalikes (amount,
date, party, governing law) are still readable. Also confirm in the PDF: the redacted text appears
as `████` blocks, and the verification report lists the checks that passed.

CLI-only variant:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe suggest testdocs\contract.pdf -o testdocs\pdf-decisions.json --policy counterparty
# set each "status" to "accepted" (or "rejected") in testdocs\pdf-decisions.json
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe redact testdocs\contract.pdf --decisions testdocs\pdf-decisions.json -o testdocs\contract.redacted.pdf
```

Try the review gate: leave one suggestion undecided and confirm export is blocked; then reject a
false positive on purpose and try drawing your own box.

## 3. Track B — scanned PDF and OCR

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract-scan.pdf
# expect: PF003 "OCR will be used", PF015/PF016 about what OCR cannot see
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe review  testdocs\contract-scan.pdf
```

Accept the suggestions, acknowledge the findings, export, then:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\check_planted_values.py testdocs\planted.json <exported>.pdf
```
Expect `PASS`, with the note "no text layer (checked by OCR)": the output page is an image with the
boxes burnt in, so it is not searchable — that is the design, not a failure.

Orientation: `inspect testdocs\contract-rotated.pdf` must show `PF017` (rotated, auto-corrected);
the review and export should still find the planted data. `--no-ocr` on any command must refuse the
scan (`PF003`, fail closed) and write nothing.

## 4. Track C — Word `.docx` (new in 0.3.0)

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract.docx
# expect REVIEW PF112 (comments will be stripped) and PF114 (custom XML will be removed)
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe suggest testdocs\contract.docx -o testdocs\docx-decisions.json --policy counterparty
```

Accept the decisions (edit the JSON, or run this one-liner)…
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('testdocs/docx-decisions.json'); d=json.loads(p.read_text()); [x.update(status='accepted') for x in d['decisions']]; p.write_text(json.dumps(d,indent=1)); print('accepted', len(d['decisions']))"
```

…then export. First **without** acknowledging the pre-flight findings — it must refuse:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe redact testdocs\contract.docx --decisions testdocs\docx-decisions.json -o testdocs\contract.redacted.docx
# expect: REFUSED: export blocked: pre-flight PF112 not acknowledged ...  and no output file
```

Then with the acknowledgements:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe redact testdocs\contract.docx --decisions testdocs\docx-decisions.json -o testdocs\contract.redacted.docx --ack PF112,PF114
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\check_planted_values.py testdocs\planted.json testdocs\contract.redacted.docx
```
Expect: `V101`–`V108` PASS, `written:`, and the checker `PASS` (no planted value anywhere in the
package, including part names and metadata).

Now open `testdocs\contract.redacted.docx` in **Word** and check:
- it opens without a "repair" prompt; the personal data is replaced by `████` blocks;
- `Ctrl+F` for each planted value finds nothing; the amount/date/party/law are intact;
- Review → Comments shows none (the comment was removed, not redacted);
- File → Info shows no author/editor (properties were emptied).

There is no browser review page for `.docx` (the page renders PDF pages); DOCX review is the
decision file, stated in the docs. Also confirm speed: a short document takes well under a second
on this machine.

## 5. Track D — things that must be refused (fail closed)

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract-tracked.docx
# expect REFUSE PF105 (tracked changes) — then redact must write nothing
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract-large-image.docx
# expect REFUSE PF123 (image covering >=25% of a page; text in pixels cannot be redacted in .docx)
```

In Word, also make and try: an encrypted copy (File → Info → Protect Document → Encrypt with
Password) → `PF101`; a macro-enabled copy saved as `.docm` → `PF103`; a legacy `.doc` → `PF102`.
In each case `redact` must exit non-zero and leave no output file.

## 6. Track E — regression and honesty checks

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q                 # 234 passed
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe bench-export --n 3     # "every injected leak caught" (13/13)
```

Optional, heavier (needs the ML extras): `legal-redact bench --suite holdout4 --detector ensemble`
runs the spent home-field suite; `legal-redact bench-h2h --suite indep --work DIR` runs the
independent-data suite (docs/BENCHMARKS.md explains what each number means, including where the
tool loses).

## 6b. Track F — custom OCR engine (new in 0.4.0)

The default engine is local Tesseract. `--ocr-engine`/`--ocr-command` plug in a
wrapper you write; docs/OCR_BACKENDS.md has the JSON contract and real examples
(paid cloud engine, local RapidOCR). The automated proof is
`tests/test_ocr_backends.py` plus `tests/fixtures/fake_ocr_engine.py`.

Make a deliberately empty but valid wrapper to try the gates. In PowerShell:

```powershell
@'
import json
# A wrapper that answers honestly: "I read nothing" (as if the page were blank).
print(json.dumps({"engine": "demo", "version": "0.1", "local": False,
                  "rotation": 0, "words": []}))
'@ | Set-Content testdocs\demo_ocr_wrapper.py
```

1. **No approval: the engine must never run.** Expect exit code 2, a disclaimer on stderr and
   nothing OCR'd:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract-scan.pdf --ocr-engine "command:.venv\Scripts\python.exe testdocs\demo_ocr_wrapper.py"
# expect: REFUSE PF020 ... cloud/third-party OCR is not approved ... docs/OCR_BACKENDS.md
```
2. **With approval:** the disclaimer is printed, `inspect` shows the engine and a REVIEW PF019:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe inspect testdocs\contract-scan.pdf --ocr-engine "command:.venv\Scripts\python.exe testdocs\demo_ocr_wrapper.py" --allow-cloud-ocr
# expect: ocr=available (engine=command ... local=no), REVIEW PF019 with the disclaimer
```
3. **Per-file acknowledgement:** `suggest` writes a decision file pinned to the cloud engine;
   `redact` must refuse until PF019 is acknowledged, then succeed:
```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe suggest testdocs\contract-scan.pdf -o testdocs\cloud-decisions.json --detector rules --ocr-engine "command:.venv\Scripts\python.exe testdocs\demo_ocr_wrapper.py" --allow-cloud-ocr
.\.venv\Scripts\legal-redact.exe redact testdocs\contract-scan.pdf --decisions testdocs\cloud-decisions.json -o testdocs\cloud.redacted.pdf --accept-proposed --ocr-engine "command:.venv\Scripts\python.exe testdocs\demo_ocr_wrapper.py" --allow-cloud-ocr
# expect: REFUSED ... PF019 not acknowledged ... and no output file
# then repeat with --ack PF019; expect the export (or "no redactions accepted" because the
# demo wrapper returned no words -- that is the honest answer for an engine that read nothing).
```
   For a fully working local custom engine, use the RapidOCR wrapper in docs/OCR_BACKENDS.md.
4. **Approval is not remembered:** repeat the `redact` command *without* `--allow-cloud-ocr`; it must
   refuse (exit 2) on the engine gate before touching the decision file.
5. **Fail closed on bad output:** change the wrapper to `print("not json")`; `inspect` must print a
   clean REFUSE with no traceback and write no output. `--ocr-engine mystery` must also refuse with a
   message naming docs/OCR_BACKENDS.md.
6. **Engine pinning:** run `suggest` with the default engine, then `redact` with
   `--ocr-engine "command:..." --allow-cloud-ocr`; it must refuse and say to re-run `suggest`
   (PF022), leaving no output file.

Track F outcome: 35 additional tests cover all of the above (232 in total).

## 8. What to report back

Highest value first:
1. a planted value **recoverable** from a redacted output (send the file and the exact string);
2. a **safe** file refused, or a refused file that still wrote an output;
3. a crash/traceback, or Word showing a repair prompt;
4. a finding/suggestion that is wrong or confusing, or a review-page/CLI usability problem;
5. your environment (Python version, ensemble or `--detector rules`, Tesseract yes/no).

Note: `--detector rules` is the fast, no-model-download path and detects only structured
identifiers (e-mail, phone, IBAN, card, DOB) — names and addresses need the ensemble. That is a
documented scope difference, not a bug.

## 9. Known gaps (do not report as bugs)

See [README Limitations](../README.md#limitations) and [docs/DOCX.md](DOCX.md#known-gaps-deliberate-documented):
NFD Unicode names; text inside images; presentation-only Word names; tracked changes and
encrypted/macro/legacy files (refused by design); DOCX batch-style review; DOCX not benchmarked;
the `pdfredeval` rendering-condition benchmark failing closed by scope.
